entries.statement: Repository-level evaluations exercise cross-file context and coordinated code changes that isolated function exercises omit.
limitations: SWE-bench studies real issue resolution and RepoBench studies repository-level completion; neither evaluates a new programming language.
Volt's synthetic maintenance corpus is narrower than either source.

entries.statement: Test-suite insufficiency can accept incorrect generated programs and can change model rankings; strengthened tests reduce that false-positive risk.
limitations: EvalPlus studies function-synthesis benchmarks, so mutation checks must be revalidated for Volt's repository tasks.

entries.statement: Code-generation performance varies across languages in ways that cannot be attributed cleanly to a single language property or popularity measure.
limitations: MultiPL-E uses translated function-level tasks rather than repository maintenance.
It motivates caution but does not quantify Volt's model-exposure confound.

entries.statement: Iterative debugging behavior can change code-generation success, so repair feedback and repair budgets belong in the treatment definition.
limitations: Self-Debugging does not isolate structured compiler diagnostics from equivalent plain-text diagnostics.
The Volt diagnostic comparison therefore remains a new causal experiment.

entries.statement: Unit-cost ordered-tree edit distance supplies a deterministic structural distance for normalized AST repair locality.
limitations: Tree edit distance is a structural proxy and is not itself a measure of semantic correctness.

entries.statement: A sequentially rejective Holm procedure controls family-wise error across the preregistered primary comparisons.
limitations: Validity still depends on the preregistered randomization and clustered analysis being implemented correctly.

entries.statement: Volt's explicit static-obligation bundle improves first-submission hidden-test pass rate by a meaningful amount.
limitations: No prior source establishes a Volt-specific causal benefit.
The bundled ablation cannot attribute an effect separately to contracts and effects.

entries.statement: Volt's canonical-only syntax improves first-submission hidden-test pass rate relative to an equally documented finite alias set.
limitations: No prior source establishes a Volt-specific causal benefit.

entries.statement: Structured DiagnosticV1 rendering improves repair success within three turns relative to plain rendering of the same facts.
limitations: No prior source isolates this representation-only effect.
The claim applies only to trajectories with the same frozen first-submission failure.
